step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Atlassian Forge's application deployment and execution workflows. There are two main flows: 1) Deployment Flow: A developer uses the CLI to send customer code (JS/TS) to an EC2 Deployment Ingestion web service sitting behind an ALB. This service records state in DynamoDB and enqueues deployment jobs into an SQS queue to handle scale and avoid Lambda control plane rate limits. An EC2 Deployment Worker polls SQS and provisions the Lambda function across an account boundary line into a separate execution account. 2) Invocation Flow: An end user's Browser calls an internal EC2 Invocation Service. This service validates security permissions, resolves the proper multi-tenant Lambda function, and invokes it (where execution occurs inside per-request V8 isolates for strict tenant isolation). All nodes and flows are mapped accurately to valid AWS and actor categories.

graph.name: Atlassian Forge Architecture
graph.notes: Atlassian Forge uses multi-tenant Lambda infrastructure separated by account boundaries and V8 isolates per request to ensure customer code security and isolate compute execution.
